messages:
acme-admin: Hey @support — our production app started getting 401 invalid_api_key when calling https://api.redwood.ai/v1/respond since yesterday after we rotated keys. SDK v1.4.1. Log shows: `{\"error\":\"invalid_api_key\",\"message\":\"API key invalid or expired\"}`. We copied the key from the Dedicated console. Any ideas?
emma-support: Thanks — can you paste the first 8 chars of the key (e.g., rwdk_...) and confirm whether you're hitting the hosted endpoint (api.redwood.ai) or a dedicated endpoint?
acme-admin: Prefix is `rd_ded_AB12CD34`. We're pointing at https://api.redwood.ai/v1/respond (hosted).
sam-eng: That explains it — `rd_ded_` is a Dedicated deploy key bound to a private/dedicated endpoint. Those keys are invalid against the hosted api.redwood.ai domain. Hosted keys typically start with `rwdk_` (or the hosted prefix for your org). Two options: 1) call your dedicated endpoint (something like https://dedicated-<org>.redwood.ai) with the `rd_ded_` key, or 2) generate a hosted API key in Dashboard > API keys and use that for api.redwood.ai.
acme-admin: Ugh — we grabbed the wrong key from the UI because the masked value looked the same. Is there a fast mitigation? We have a release in ~30m.
liam-sre: Fastest fix: create a new hosted key and inject it into your k8s secret (REDWOOD_API_KEY) then restart the pods. If you need to keep using the dedicated key for other services, make sure the SDK endpoint/host env var points to your dedicated host. Quick repro commands:

Wrong (will 401 with a dedicated key against hosted):
```
curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer rd_ded_AB12CD34' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/respond -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```

Correct (hosted key against hosted):
```
curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer rwdk_xxxYOURHOSTEDKEY' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/respond -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
emma-support: I filed a support ticket and added a quick note in the docs about key prefixes. @product — would be great to add a UI hint when copying keys (label hosted vs dedicated).
deploy-bot: ticket #SUP-12345 created; assigned to support.
acme-admin: Thanks — generated a hosted key, updated the secret, rolled the deployment, and the 401s stopped. All green.
sam-eng: Awesome — marking this as resolved from engineering side. Recommendation: add a CI check that validates a 200/200-like response from a small generate/health call after key rotations so this doesn't slip through.
